alt: The Tang line holds the narrow mouth of the White River over the sandbars
scene: Morning before the battle, low over the water from a sandbar at the waterline, wet reeds blurred in the foreground. The Tang line fills the frame as one long dark wall of anchored tower-ships across the river throat, hull after hull receding into haze, crossbowmen small along every bulwark, red banners snapping in a hard sea wind, anchor cables taut and dripping. Far out on the bright sea the first specks of the Yamato boats. Tension, not calm: men on the nearest deck pointing out to sea, an officer shouting down the line. PLACE (match the attached pl_white_river board and the battle map): the wide grey-brown mouth of the White River, low blue hills on both banks, tidal mudflats, shifting sandbars and reed beds. The Tang fleet of 170 dark tower-ships and warships lies anchored in ONE tight line across the narrow throat of the river, bows to the sea; the Yamato and Baekje boats come in from the open sea to the south-west, hundreds of small open rowing boats packed together. Alongside, a Tang deck stands a man’s height above any Yamato boat; the Tang broadside is a wooden wall the Yamato boats break on. BANNERS BY SIDE: vermilion Tang banners fly ONLY on the dark Tang hulls; red Wa sunburst banners ONLY on the Yamato boats; Tang sails are plain deep red, no emblem; the Tang sun disc holds an abstract black smudge, never a readable character.
